paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: we make the plans, but the LORD is the One in charge. Solomon says it plain in Proverbs 16:9: "A man's heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps." I had a whole life planned on that kitchen counter, and a cookie planet was NOT on the list (and I'm so glad He had better ideas). So make your plans, but hold them with open hands.

Now, how do you live with that? Solomon gives the answer in Proverbs 16:3: "Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved." He also warns that "There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death" (Proverbs 16:25). Your own eyes can lie to you, friend, so hand your plans to the One who weighs motives (Proverbs 16:2).

The rest of the chapter shows what that kind of life looks like. It means wisdom over gold (Proverbs 16:16), humility over pride (Proverbs 16:18), and pleasant words that are "sweet to the soul and healing to the bones" (Proverbs 16:24). It even means a calm temper, because "he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city" (Proverbs 16:32). And when life feels like a roll of the dice, remember that "its every decision is from the LORD" (Proverbs 16:33).
